responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the DEC/Compaq Alpha architecture and its OS/ABI variants. It defines the Alpha machine model used during late compilation and code generation: the core target headers and implementation files establish architectural properties, calling conventions, register usage, address and constant legality, option handling, builtin expansion, prologue/epilogue generation, assembler syntax, and target-specific RTL passes; the main machine description, predicates, constraints, synchronization patterns, and extra mode definitions map generic GCC RTL onto Alpha instructions, operand classes, atomic ll/sc sequences, and floating/vector mode support; the EV4/EV5/EV6 scheduling descriptions tune instruction ordering for specific processors; the driver helper handles native CPU detection for -mcpu/-mtune; and the ELF, Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, and OpenVMS headers layer in object-format, linker, runtime, and ABI policy differences. Together these files make this module the architecture-specific code generation, scheduling, and platform-integration layer for Alpha, distinguishing it from generic RTL middle-end modules and from backends for other targets.
